statement: The quartic $x^{4}+px^{3}+qx^{2}+rx+s$ is divisible by the quadratic $x^{2}+ax+b$, whose roots are also roots of the quartic. Show that the remaining two roots satisfy $x^{2}+(p-a)x+(a^{2}-ap-b+q)=0$.
solution: Write $x^{4}+px^{3}+qx^{2}+rx+s=(x^{2}+ax+b)(x^{2}+(p-a)x+c)$. Expanding: $x^{4}+px^{3}+(c+a(p-a)+b)x^{2}+(ac+b(p-a))x+bc$. Matching $x^{2}$: $q=c+a(p-a)+b$, so $c=a^{2}-ap-b+q$. Thus the other factor is $x^{2}+(p-a)x+(a^{2}-ap-b+q)$, giving the stated equation.
